title: SplitScope: rollout inspector for canary/A-B/shadow traffic
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: teams running model rollouts (canary, A/B, shadow) lack a single place in Console to quickly compare candidate variants, inspect representative traces, and decide whether to promote or invoke auto-rollback. Existing views are scattered: per-route time-series, raw traces, and separate deployment pages. This ticket defines SplitScope — a unified inspector that surfaces paired comparisons, trace-linked sample diffs, and a configurable auto-rollback confidence editor.
goals: Create a side-by-side metric diff panel for two or more rollout variants showing absolute and relative change with statistical significance guidance
Add trace-linked sample viewer that pulls representative requests (low-latency sample) and highlights token-level divergence and prefix/KV cache effects
Expose per-route and per-model telemetry (latency P50/P95, tail-latency, error-rate, token-cost) and traffic weighting controls for on-console experiment adjustments
Provide a safe auto-rollback policy editor (thresholds, cooldowns, guardrail metrics) and a dry-run mode for simulated rollbacks
Support shadow replay sink links and a sandboxed replay runner to diagnose divergences without affecting production
acceptance_criteria: Console UI shows a split comparison view for an active rollout with selectable baseline and candidate variants
Metric diffs display delta, percent change, and a simple significance indicator (green/amber/red) with drill-to-timeseries
Clicking a metric opens a list of traced request samples; selecting a sample shows side-by-side model outputs and token-level divergence highlights
Auto-rollback editor persists policies to the rollout config and evaluates dry-run simulations on historical windows
Shadow replay link launches a replay job in the sandbox project and surfaces a summarized divergence report

Design: hi-fi mockups of split comparator, sample viewer, and rollback editor (Figma link below)
Backend: add variant pairing API, aggregated delta calculation endpoint, and sample extraction index

risks: Sampling bias: small sample sets could give false signals — mitigated by configurable sample window and confidence warnings
Performance: computing deltas for high-cardinality routes could be slow — mitigate via pre-aggregation and cached summaries
Operator error: accidental rollback due to UI mis-click — mitigate with confirm flows, cooldowns, and dry-run default
